global.gamma: gamma(m) = m*u32/(1 - m*u32) (handoff section 7); requires m*u32 < 1

metrics.max_rel: max_i |y_i - r_i| / max(|r_i|, floor), floor = 1e-6 * rms(r) unless stated
metrics.nrmse: ||y - r||_2 / ||r||_2 over the compared tensor (per row when rows are stated)
metrics.bound_ratio: max_i |y_i - r_i| / B_i for the named worst-case bound B
metrics.prob_exceed: count_i(|y_i - r_i| > P_i) for the named probabilistic bound P (lambda = 6)
metrics.nonfinite: count of NaN/Inf in y where r is finite (any > 0 fails)
metrics.ulp: distance in units in the last place of the output format

global.reference_precision: float64 for all arithmetic; exact integer arithmetic for structure; model-defined FP8/FP4 quantize-dequantize steps are applied exactly (round-to-nearest-even) because they are part of the model function, not a precision choice
global.re_anchoring: Operator and layer gates compare like with like: the GPU result is compared with the reference evaluated on the GPU's own inputs (its input tensors converted exactly to float64), or the GPU is fed the reference fixture inputs. Operator budgets never apply to free-running trajectories; the full trace has its own section.
global.declared_path: Each GPU kernel's manifest entry declares its precision path: operand formats (e.g. activations rounded to fp16/bf16/kept fp32), accumulator format, reduction length m (K for one sequential sum; K/S + S for split-K into S partials; ceil(log2 K) + leaf length for trees; acc = fp32_wmma for WMMA accumulation, see wmma_rule), output format. The bound functions take exactly these parameters. An undeclared path is evaluated with the most pessimistic listed option and flagged.
global.nan_contract: Every exact (class A) gate compares NaN as a class: an output that should be NaN must be NaN (any payload, quiet or signalling bit as produced), and nothing else may be NaN; finite values and +-inf must match bit for bit with round-to-nearest-even. Reason: the AMD f32->bf16 conversions (w-arch glue.hip, w-tri aux.hip) keep the NaN payload, (bits >> 16) | 0x40, where CUDA's cvt.rn.bf16.f32 returns a canonical NaN; both are correct conversions. Numerical (class B) gates already fail on any unexpected nonfinite value.

wmma_rule.finding: On gfx1151 the WMMA fp32 accumulation is not round-to-nearest-even: an identity matrix times B returns B - 1 ulp where B < 0 (w-tri, node1:~/tfp/tri/results/t_wmma.jsonl, kernel wmma_f32_16x16x16_bf16, case 'I @ B for B < 0 (rounding probe)': exact false, max_ulps_off 1; random bf16 products stay within gamma_16, max_err_over_bound 0.066; kernel_status.json pass)
wmma_rule.rule: No exact (class A) gate may route through a WMMA instruction: a WMMA product is never compared bit for bit, not even against a CUDA build or another WMMA kernel. Kernels built on WMMA (w-tri's HIP sparse attention; EXL3 prefill / small-row GEMMs that use it) are graded only by their error-bound contracts, with the accumulation declared as acc = 'fp32_wmma' (dsref/bounds.py U['fp32_wmma'] = 2^-23: faithful rounding, < 1 ulp a step, twice the RNE unit roundoff). Exact gates stay on non-WMMA steps: EXL3 decode to W_inner, format conversions, quantizers re-anchored on the GPU's own pre-quantization values, index sets judged by topk_sets, token accounting.
wmma_rule.wmma_audit: Every operator contract that a WMMA-capable kernel can implement already accepts by bounds: exl3.linear and exl3.experts_grouped (worst-case + probabilistic + statistical), attention.sparse (attention_bound; its index lists are exact but are inputs, not products), indexer.topk (score bound + set rule), dense.linear_blas (bounds; its rerun-identity check is determinism, which non-RNE accumulation does not break), mhc.mixes_sinkhorn, router.noaux_tc, rmsnorm, rope. The exact contracts (exl3.codebook_mul1 / trellis_unpack / reconstruct_inner, conversion.float_formats, quant.kv_fp8 / quant.fp4, dspark.acceptance) involve no matrix product. A kernel that fuses a WMMA product into an exact step (e.g. an FP8 quantizer fed by a WMMA GEMM) is graded on the quantizer's own input as re-anchored, never on the fused output bit for bit.

bounded_replay.what: Decoder SWA Bounded Replay: a prompt runs the decoder layers (20-39, the upper half of the Causal Encoder-Decoder) only on its last window (128) of rows; a query at position i attends to window keys in [max(s, i - 127), i] with s = prompt length - 128 (DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash tech report 2.2 and 3.2.2, fixtures/replay_provenance.json). DeepSeek states it is not mathematically equivalent to a full decoder pass, of negligible quality impact, and simulated during post-training. The official inference/model.py (a readable reference, not a serving engine) has none.
bounded_replay.served: TensorFold applies it always (prompt.replayCut at layers / 2; the layer gate's prompt length is every Model.forward row before the first round); ds4 has it as an opt-in, off by default
bounded_replay.graded_semantics: The port is graded against the served semantics (integration owner, 2026-10-19): layer fixtures and the full trace come from reference traces with the floor (run_trace.py --replay rounds|prompt; dsref/refmodel.py REPLAY, tests/test_replay.py: window slots below the floor dropped at decoder layers only). Fixtures from a full-prefill trace mark the affected rows inexact_rows, reported and never gated.
bounded_replay.quality_gap: model.py full prefill vs bounded replay is measured on the reference itself (tools/replay_gap_long.py, fixtures/replay_gap.json): last-row KL/top-1 and 256-token teacher-forced continuations (KL, top-1, paired NLL change with 95% CIs) at 1K-16K prompts, prose and code. It is a property of the model's design, reported to the owner; it is not a GPU error budget and never widens one.

global.pass_rule: A gate passes only if expected_cases > 0, every expected case ran (executed == expected), the compared element count is > 0, nonfinite == 0 and every acceptance clause holds. A skipped, stubbed or zero-case run fails coverage. A kernel is never compared only with itself or another version of itself.

ambiguity_rule.topk_sets: For a top-k over scores s (reference) with a per-position error band b (b_t bounds |s_gpu,t - s_ref,t|, from the operator's probabilistic bound (lambda = 6) where numerics.json defines one, else its worst-case bound, counted for both sides): let c be the k-th largest reference score and b_c its band. Positions with s_t > c + b_t + b_c must be selected, positions with s_t < c - b_t - b_c must not be, positions in between are ambiguous and either choice is accepted provided the selected count is exactly k (the handoff's kth vs (k+1)th margin against the sum of their bounds, applied to every position). Exact ties at c (common with fp4-quantized indexer operands and with relu zeros) are ambiguous by this rule. Rows with any ambiguous position are counted and logged with their scores; the reference is already FP64, so 'recompute at higher precision' is the reference itself. Implementation: dsref/bounds.py topk_consistent.
ambiguity_rule.argmax: Same rule with k = 1: if r_(1) - r_(2) > b_(1) + b_(2) the GPU argmax must equal the reference argmax; otherwise the position is ambiguous and logged. torch argmax/topk tie order is unspecified in model.py, so no tie-break is imposed on exact ties.
ambiguity_rule.quantizers: FP8/FP4 quantize-dequantize: an element whose scaled value x/s lies within its input error band of a rounding midpoint may round either way; a block whose amax/qmax lies within its band of a power of two (UE8M0 scales) or an E4M3 midpoint (E4M3 scales) may take either scale. Everything else must be bit-exact.
ambiguity_rule.unexplained: Any changed discrete decision outside the ambiguous set fails the gate.

global.fixture_provenance: Every fixture records source commit (ref git), checkpoint revision, input token ids / input bytes (sha256), dtype, generation method and the numerics.json version it was produced under (run_trace.py manifest.json).
global.budget_change_policy: A budget or acceptance change is a review item, bumps `version`, and invalidates prior passes. Raising a tolerance is never a fix by itself; a failure is diagnosed first.

operators.computation: 16-bit trellis state s -> fp16: x = (s * 0x83DCD12D) mod 2^32; h = fp16(0x6400 + bytesum(x)) = 1024 + bytesum; v = RNE_fp16(h * fp16(0x1EEE) + fp16(0xC931)) with one rounding (fused multiply-add) = RNE_fp16((1774 h - 2721792) * 2^-18)

operators.rounding_reduction: integer ops exact; one RNE rounding to fp16. Note: an fp32 FMA followed by fp16 rounding is also exact for all states (0 mismatches); a separate fp16 multiply then fp16 add is wrong for 60,326 states

operators.computation: Tile of 256 weights stored as 16*K uint16 (K = bits, 1..8). Stream = the tile's little-endian uint32 words, each read MSB first (pack.cu SWAP16). State of element e = stream bits [(e+1)K-16, (e+1)K) modulo 256K (tail-biting). Element e goes to tile position perm[e] (quantize.py tensor_core_perm: for t = e//8, r0 = (t%4)*2, c0 = t//4, the 8 elements of t go to (r0,c0),(r0+1,c0),(r0+8,c0),(r0+9,c0),(r0,c0+8),(r0+1,c0+8),(r0+8,c0+8),(r0+9,c0+8)). trellis[a, b] is the tile at rows 16a (in_features), cols 16b (out_features).

procedure: 1. Inputs from the GPU debug dump: its router input x (the ffn_norm output in the GPU's storage dtype), its selected experts S_gpu and routing weights w_gpu, per row.
2. Recompute the reference on x exactly converted to float64: logits = x W^T with the pack's F16 gate weight, score = sqrt(softplus(logits)), biased = score + pack F16 bias (model.py Gate.forward).
3. Band per expert e: b_e = 2 * (softplus_sqrt_bound(logit_e, dot_prob_bound(x, W_e, in_fmt = declared router-input format, acc = fp32)) + u32 |biased_e|) (dsref/bounds.py; 2x covers both sides).

4. Classify the row with c = 6th largest reference biased score (3rd for DSpark) and b_c its band: MUST = {e: biased_e > c + b_e + b_c}, FREE = {e: |biased_e - c| <= b_e + b_c, e not in MUST}. Unambiguous row: |FREE| == 6 - |MUST|, so S_gpu must equal the reference set exactly. Ambiguous row: |FREE| > 6 - |MUST|; accept S_gpu iff MUST is a subset of S_gpu, S_gpu is a subset of MUST union FREE, and |S_gpu| == 6.

5. Recomputation: the FP64 reference is the higher-precision recomputation (its own error, ~1e-13 relative, is far below any band); scores equal in FP64 to within 1e-12 relative are exact ties and either order is accepted. No further tie-break is imposed (model.py uses torch.topk, which does not specify one).

6. Weights: for rows with S_gpu == S_ref check |w_gpu - w_ref| against the weights clause; for accepted ambiguous rows with S_gpu != S_ref check w_gpu against the reference weights computed for S_gpu from the same reference scores.

7. Never substitute: the reference trace keeps its own selection (handoff section 7). Rows where the GPU legitimately chose differently inside the band are excluded from that layer's MoE-output numerical metric, counted, and reported with their margins; a selection outside the rule fails the gate.
8. Separately (not graded) report what the official-F32 gate would have chosen on the same inputs (tools/router_official_diff.py).

Separate report, never a gate (tools/router_official_diff.py, fixtures/router_official_diff_*.json): on identical router inputs the official F32 gate picks a different expert set on 7.8-8.6% of rows (173/2004 rows at P=160, 1035/13284 at P=1100 over the 12 fixture layers), all with pack 6th/7th margins <= 0.025. layer_points.metric: per point (one step, one layer, one rank where ranked): nrmse and worst token-row nrmse (a gather's token rows are its second axis) against the FP64 truth must stay under 'nrmse' and 'row_nrmse'; scale_err = |median of (got - ref) / ref| over the elements at or above rms(ref) under 'scale_err'; the median nrmse over all points of the type under 'nrmse_median'; nonfinite per global.nan_contract; rows the harness did not run (its dump's row_start, which must equal the fixture's replay_row_start) are not graded; rows whose expert set differs inside the router band are excluded from moe_partial, moe_gather(_in), h_out, pre_out and route_wts and counted; routing itself is graded by the router.noaux_tc procedure on the GPU's own moe_in rows

These gates catch layout, partition, missing-term and sign bugs; scaling errors of a percent and below are the operator replay's (op_points)
